details: The image equivalent of tokenization: fixed-size patches (e.g. 14x14 pixels) projected into embedding vectors. Image resolution therefore translates directly into token count and cost in VLMs.

explainer.lead: Patch embedding is the image counterpart of tokenization: the image is cut into fixed-size patches that are projected into embedding vectors. It matters because image resolution translates directly into token count and therefore cost in vision-language models.

tiers.eli5: Tear a photo into a grid of equal squares, then turn each square into a short summary card the model can read; a bigger photo means more cards.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick patch size and input resolution to trade detail against compute and context length. The pitfall is that large inputs explode the token count, so high-resolution images can blow up latency and cost.
tiers.paperLevel: A patch of p x p pixels is flattened and linearly projected into an embedding vector; the number of tokens is (image width / p) times (image height / p). The token count therefore grows with the square of resolution.

explainer.example: A 224x224 image with 14x14 patches yields 16x16 = 256 patch embeddings, one token per patch fed to the transformer.
